raw_segments.text: From 1621 to 1636, both inclusive, the average price of the same measure of the best wheat,

at the same market, appears, from the same accounts, to have been £ 2,10s.; from which, making the like deductions as in the foregoing case, the average price of the quarter of eight bushels of middle wheat comes out to have been £ 1, 19, 6, or about seven ounces and two-thirds of an ounce of silver.
From 1621 to 1636, both inclusive, the average price of the same measure of the best wheat,
at the same market, appears from the same accounts to have been two—tens.
From which, making the like deductions as in the foregoing case, the average price of
the quarter of eight bushels of middle wheat comes out to have been one—nineteen, six,
or about seven ounces and two-thirds of an ounce of silver.
